newsitem.title: UK: Gen Accident lays out acqusition strategy.
newsitem.headline: Gen Accident lays out acqusition strategy.

text.p: British composite insurer General Accident (GA) has specified for the first time it is looking to buy two companies, one dealing in life and the other a general insurance concern with small business expertise.
GA, which has assets of 28.2 billion pounds ($46.2 billion), expects an increase this year of at least 20 percent and possibly as much as 35 percent in new life premium income.
It is part of a three-year strategy to double business from sales of life assurance, pensions and investment products.
Philip Twyman, executive director in charge of finance and life operations, said the two acquisitions were needed to fulfil his company's objectives and to keep up with competitors.
"As some of the other insurance people get bigger we need to keep up with them," he said.
However, despite this pressure GA said it would not be rushed into any snap decisions over the acquisitions.

"Just as our 170 million pound Provident Mutual purchase last year was a well thought out move and we wanted them before they wanted us, so these next two prospective buys will be treated similarly," he said.
GA is currently scrutinising the market to identify companies that offer the best strategic fit to the Perth-based company's future needs.
Certain companies up for sales will not fit the GA criteria. "There will be nothing wrong with them but they will not be for us."

Twyman and his chief executive Bob Scott formed a new-style management committee last year. One of its aims is to work out how GA can generate new premium income sales from its life assurance, pensions and investment products.
Twyman confirmed the firm is looking to target a life company whilst on the general insurance front a company with small business expertise is sought.

"We have recognised that the small business commercial sector represents an economic growth area and you need a particular skill to reach them," Twyman explained. There are companies out there with this expertise."
Growth of between 20 and 35 percent was not a tall order he said. "0ur life company in the first quarter was up 48 percent in pensions and 18 percent in overall sales."
Last week GA announced first-quarter, pre-tax profits of 114 million pounds compared with last year's weather-depressed profits of 55 million pounds.
